hints: Focus on how many bonding pairs and lone pairs are on nitrogen in $\text{NH}_3$ compared to $\text{NH}_4^+$.
Remember $\text{NH}_3$ has three N-H bonds plus one lone pair, while $\text{NH}_4^+$ has four N-H bonds and no lone pair.
Think about whether a single N-H bond formed by direct head-on overlap is sigma or pi, including the dative bond in ammonium.
walkthrough:
**Count electron pairs on nitrogen**

Think of nitrogen as the centre holding all the pairs. In $\text{NH}_3$, nitrogen has 3 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair. In $\text{NH}_4^+$, the lone pair is used to form a dative bond to $\text{H}^+$, so nitrogen has 4 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs.

$$\text{NH}_3: 3 \text{ bond pairs } + 1 \text{ lone pair} \quad , \quad \text{NH}_4^+: 4 \text{ bond pairs } + 0 \text{ lone pairs}$$

**Predict the shapes**

A lone pair pushes the bonds closer together. So 3 bonds plus 1 lone pair gives trigonal pyramidal for ammonia, while 4 bonds with no lone pair gives a perfect regular tetrahedral arrangement for ammonium.

$$4 \text{ electron pairs } \rightarrow \text{ tetrahedral basis, lone pair makes } \text{NH}_3 \text{ pyramidal}$$

**Identify the bond type**

Every N-H single bond is formed by end-on overlap of orbitals along the bond axis. That is the definition of a sigma bond, and the dative covalent bond in $\text{NH}_4^+$ is also just a sigma bond once formed.

$$\text{all N-H single bonds} = \sigma \text{ only, no } \pi$$

options.A: This is correct. Ammonia is pyramidal due to 3 bond pairs and 1 lone pair, ammonium is regular tetrahedral due to 4 bond pairs, and all N-H single bonds including the dative bond are sigma bonds.
options.B: Shapes are correct but the bond for ammonium is wrong. Students choose this if they think the dative or coordinate bond is a pi bond. Once formed, it is identical to the other three sigma N-H bonds.
options.C: Bonds are correct but shapes are swapped. Ammonia cannot be regular tetrahedral because its lone pair distorts the shape to pyramidal, and ammonium cannot be pyramidal because it has four equal bonding pairs.
options.D: Both parts are wrong. Ammonia is not tetrahedral and its N-H bonds are not pi bonds. Pi bonds only occur in multiple bonds, never in single N-H bonds.
